bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to local government; allowing local government noncompliance with unfunded mandates; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 373; 471.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[373.52] NO MANDATES WITHOUT FUNDING. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+County noncompliance allowed.+]

[+(a) Except as provided under subdivision 2, a county is not required to comply with a state mandate in paragraph (b) until a state law provides a county with the amount of revenue needed to pay for the mandate. +]

[+(b) A state mandate that a county is not required to comply with under paragraph (a) is a mandate that: +]

[+(1) affects the daily operation of a county government; +]

[+(2) changes the allocation of a county's resources; or +]

[+(3) changes a county's spending priorities. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Exceptions.+]

[+A county must comply with a state mandate if the amount of revenue needed for compliance is incidental compared to the county's total budget. A county must continue compliance with any law that governs financial audit requirements or that directly affects the safety and health of county residents. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section applies to state mandates that are in effect after June 30, 2025. +]

Sec. 2.

[+[471.343] NO MANDATES WITHOUT FUNDING. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Municipal noncompliance allowed.+]

[+(a) Except as provided under subdivision 2, a municipality is not required to comply with a state mandate in paragraph (b) until a state law provides a municipality with the amount of revenue needed to pay for the mandate. +]

[+(b) A state mandate that a municipality is not required to comply with under paragraph (a) is a mandate that: +]

[+(1) affects the daily operation of municipal government; +]

[+(2) changes the allocation of municipal resources; or +]

[+(3) changes a municipality's spending priorities. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Exceptions.+]

[+A municipality must comply with a state mandate if the amount of revenue needed for compliance is incidental compared to the municipality's total budget. A municipality must continue compliance with any law that governs financial audit requirements or that directly affects the safety and health of municipal residents. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section applies to state mandates that are in effect after June 30, 2025. +]
